Jamie Dimon, the head of JPMorgan Chase, once called Bitcoin a fraud and said he would fire any employee caught buying it.

At that exact same time, he and his associates were buying cryptocurrency through other companies.

If you had ignored his warning and put $1,000 into Bitcoin that day, you would have $14,547.40 today.

Kevin Trudeau has pointed out for years that the people warning you off an opportunity are often the ones quietly taking it for themselves.

So who's really the fool here?

Steve Jobs swore by a simple 10 minute rule, and modern neuroscience is now confirming he was right.

When you're stuck on a hard decision, the fix isn't to push harder. It's to step outside, go for a walk, and look at things far away.

That simple habit relaxes the brain, lowers stress, and clears the way to the answer you were missing.

Kevin Trudeau points out that wealthy people have quietly done this for centuries whenever they hit a wall.

What's stopping you from trying it today?
